<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/plugin-hono-server`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **8** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/security/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**17** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e40f2df2990d8bda0ae02cda0d4d41b44216e16f`.

⛔ **5** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/security/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **183** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e40f2df2990d8bda0ae02cda0d4d41b44216e16f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e93911cc925689da02d4d907f39257a6ac1010c9` — the merge of head `028060723d1ca4f4a4c85ee075c0fec70021bb34` into base `e40f2df2990d8bda0ae02cda0d4d41b44216e16f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e93911cc925689da02d4d907f39257a6ac1010c9 && git checkout e93911cc925689da02d4d907f39257a6ac1010c9
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e40f2df2990d8bda0ae02cda0d4d41b44216e16f 028060723d1ca4f4a4c85ee075c0fec70021bb34 && git checkout -B drift-repro e40f2df2990d8bda0ae02cda0d4d41b44216e16f && git merge --no-ff 028060723d1ca4f4a4c85ee075c0fec70021bb34

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e40f2df2990d8bda0ae02cda0d4d41b44216e16f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e40f2df2990d8bda0ae02cda0d4d41b44216e16f` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

security#2 · os-justin · session_01QSeKYn5CmmdShCJifm6WYj

The seat adopts the record below, rendered on this head by an isolated reviewer at the contract-review tier.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f1b9c6b7bab349612406af5580efb0cd8d070643`
Local-runs: none
Scope: docs/adr/0142-ownership-queue-membership-claim-and-assignment-rules.md + packages/core/src/security/effective-object-permissions.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/explain-engine.ts, .changeset/explain-transfer-composes-edit.md, content/docs/permissions/explain.mdx, packages/core/src/security/effective-object-permissions.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/explain-engine.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/explain-enforce-parity.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/get-effective-object-permissions.test.ts

The read-only shape held. Inputs read:
- the diff `origin/main...origin/claude/sec2-hjqw-1b` (merge-base `45f0f81fb0`);
- the tree at this head;
- ruling record 6755714726;
- the head's check-runs.

Check-runs at read time: 45 total, 14 success, 9 skipped, 22 in progress, 0 failed. Every `Test Core` shard, the type-check jobs and most lint jobs were still running, so this record observed no suite result on this head.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`security.explain`, `operation: 'transfer'`, `object_crud` layer: narrowed. Right.**
   - The layer now grants only where the same set list both grants edit and holds the transfer grant, for the agent and for the delegator.
   - Edit from one set and the grant from another compose.
   - A principal holding the grant without edit gets its own denial sentence.
   - The record-grained verdict follows the layer.

   This is the ruling's first sentence, and it matches the owner-change door as the tree builds it.
2. **`/me/permissions` `objects[*].allowTransfer`: narrowed on every object, the `*` entry included. Right for the client hint.** Only a `true` bit is lowered, and no key is added. `modifyAllRecords` keeps transfer because it grants edit. The ruling names this surface.
3. **`current_user.can(object, 'transfer')`: narrowed by the same map. NOT derivable from the ruling.** See ③ F1.
4. **Enforcement: unchanged in the tree.**
   - No evaluator file and no authorization-middleware file is in the diff.
   - The evaluator's `transfer` cell and the ownership step still read the transfer grant alone.
   - The parity file pins the create-and-assign insert as admitted without edit, and refused without the grant.
5. **Tests.** The `can()`-versus-evaluator parity battery is re-pinned for `transfer`: it compared against the evaluator cell and now compares against edit ∧ cell. That is the pin item 3 moves, and it stands or falls with F1. Three existing core fixtures gained `allowEdit` so they keep pinning what they were written for; that is acceptable.
6. **No schema, export or type changes.** `GRANT_BITS`, the spec fold and the explain vocabulary are untouched.

### ② Semver level

- `patch` on `@objectstack/plugin-security` and `@objectstack/core`, with the BREAKING banner, an ADR-0087 marker (`no-migration-prescription`) and migration text. That is the level a non-protocol narrowing takes.
- `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is present in the PR body and the changeset, and the arm is correct.
- `Metadata-protocol: none` is correct only if `can()` does not move. If the single map is kept, the meaning of an authored expression (`current_user.can(object, 'transfer')`) changes. That is the `semantic` kind, which takes at least `minor` on the packages the diff moves. So this line and the level are bound to F1, whichever way F1 is resolved.

### ③ Boundary flags

**F1, must-fix: the `can('transfer')` narrowing is outside "Enforcement is unchanged".**

The ruling names three carriers: explain, the client permission hint, and the design record's mapping text. It does not name the server-side expression predicate. In the tree, the same map answers `current_user.can()` on the server write path in three places:
- a per-option `visibleWhen`, where a predicate answering `false` refuses the write that picks that option;
- a CEL `defaultValue`, which decides the stored value;
- a `formula` field, which decides the computed value.

For a principal holding the transfer grant without edit, each of these answers differently after this change. The first changes what the server admits. It does so on insert too, the path where that same principal can still create and assign: an option an author gated on `can(object, 'transfer')`, to offer assigning to another owner, is now refused to the one principal the owner step admits. That is a change in server behaviour on authored metadata, not a hint. The changeset's own migration text concedes that the reader "needs its own reading", and it offers no replacement predicate.

The PR needs one of:
- **(B) the split.** The clamp applies to what `/me/permissions` serves, and the map handed to the expression evaluator keeps the evaluator-cell answer. The `can()` parity battery then returns to its previous comparison.
- **(A) a maintainer ruling of record on #32004 that names `can()`.** The ADR note and the changeset then state it, and `Metadata-protocol` is re-judged per ②.

This reviewer cannot pick A, because the ruling's text does not reach it.

**F2, note: pre-existing, not graded against this diff.**
- For a queue claim, the door admits an update of the owner without the transfer grant.
- Explain's `object_crud` layer still denies `transfer` for that claimant, as it did before. The claim is carried by its own attribution, which is the only thing the Console's claim affordance reads.
- The ruling's "only where" holds, and this change makes the claim case no worse.

### ④ Design judgment

**The ADR-0142 amendment against the ruling.** The Status entry and the dated note in Context §1 state the rule as ruled, cite the record, and keep the insert case. Against its first consumer (D4 claim, "explainable as `transfer`"), nothing regresses; see F2. Findings:
- **should-fix.** The amended mapping sentence anchors "resolves to the edit grant and the `allowTransfer` grant bit together" to `effective-object-permissions.ts#GRANT_BITS`. That symbol is an unchanged list and composes nothing. The composition lives in `clampTransferToEdit` (the map) and in `explain-engine.ts#objectGrantOf` (explain). Re-anchor the sentence so the governed text points at the code that makes it true.
- **should-fix, bound to F1.** The note says "Enforcement is unchanged" and is silent on `can()`. Under A it must say that the expression predicate narrows. Under B it is true as written.
- **nit.** The D4 text could say that a claim stays reported through its own reason, not through the `object_crud` verdict.

**Break attempts.**
- **Insert-time create-and-assign broken?** No. The owner step is untouched, the control test pins it, and the UI `create` field question is not narrowed. The one exception is an authored option gated on `can(…, 'transfer')`; that is F1.
- **Evaluator fold or step 3.5 changed?** No. Neither file is in the diff. The composition is local to the explain helper and the map clamp.
- **Explain disagreeing with the door?** None introduced. Both halves are asked of the same set list, as the door asks them. Under delegation both principals need both halves, as at the door. The existing under-report for a claim is F2.
- **`*` entry or clamp ordering wrong?** No.
  - The clamp runs after every step that can remove edit: wildcard materialisation, the super-user fold, the managed-write clamp and the external-write clamp. Nothing after it removes read or edit from a surviving entry.
  - Edit is read through the spec fold, so the read half and `modifyAllRecords` are honoured.
  - A cross-set case composes: edit named on an object by one set, and the transfer grant on another set's plain wildcard. Materialisation precedes the clamp.
- **A consumer of the hint that misbehaves?** None found in `ui/`.
  - The owner-field `write` question already required the object grant for an update after the transfer grant.
  - The create form does not read the hint for the owner.
  - The claim affordance reads the claim attribution only.
  - The access panel shows the composed answer.
- **A consumer of `can()` that misbehaves?** Yes: the server-side predicates. This is F1.

Smaller findings:
- **nit.** When edit's read half and its grant half come from different sets, the granted sentence can name an empty edit list. The plain `update` explanation already behaves this way.
- **nit.** `packages/core/CHANGELOG.md` and the spec fold's jsdoc still describe the map's `transfer` as the evaluator cell. A cross-reference to the new clamp would keep readers from the old reading.

The narrowing on explain and on the client hint makes the door's own refusal visible, and that part is sound. The verdict rests on F1 alone.

security#2 · os-justin · session_01QSeKYn5CmmdShCJifm6WYj

The seat adopts the delta record below. The same isolated reviewer rendered it on this head at the contract-review tier.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `4e69ae05c28bf6cda327f924d1d6b3c1ce0696cc`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/contracts/security-service.ts, docs/adr/0142-ownership-queue-membership-claim-and-assignment-rules.md + packages/core/src/security/effective-object-permissions.ts, packages/core/src/security/index.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/current-user-endpoints.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/explain-engine.ts, .changeset/explain-transfer-composes-edit.md, content/docs/permissions/explain.mdx, packages/core/src/security/effective-object-permissions.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/current-user-endpoints-effective-objects.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/get-effective-object-permissions.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/explain-engine.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/explain-enforce-parity.test.ts

This is a delta record on the FAIL at `f1b9c6b7ba` (comment 6765422153). It reads:
- the delta `f1b9c6b7ba..4e69ae05c2` (three commits);
- the tree at this head;
- the replaced PR body;
- the head's check-runs: 68 total, 58 success, 10 skipped, 0 failed, 0 in progress.

Nothing was built or run locally.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **F1 (the server-side predicate) is closed in code.**
   - `buildEffectiveObjectPermissions` is, statement for statement, the function on the merge-base. The only code added to its file is the clamp helper and the new export.
   - The service that feeds `current_user.can()` on the server still returns that map.
   - The `can()`-versus-evaluator parity battery has no modified line against the merge-base; there is only a new describe beside it.
   - So a principal holding the transfer grant without edit gets the same server answer as on `main` in an option's `visibleWhen`, a CEL `defaultValue` and a `formula`.
   - The new pins hold this at three levels: the expression, the evaluator cell and the real endpoint.
2. **The served slot is narrowed, as the ruling names it.** `/auth/me/permissions` serves `servedObjectPermissions(…)` of the one map: a copy in which `allowTransfer` follows edit on every entry, the `*` entry included. The endpoint test pins the body byte-equal to that derivation, and equal to the base entry in every other key. This is right.
3. **New public export `servedObjectPermissions` (`@objectstack/core`).** It is additive, it does not mutate its input (pinned), and it is small and single-purpose. Its one caller in the tree is the endpoint. This is right.
4. **Explain is untouched by the delta.** The earlier judgment stands.
5. **Enforcement is unchanged.** No evaluator or authorization-middleware file is in the diff against `main`.
6. **One accept-set consequence is not stated anywhere in the public text.** The Console evaluates authored `current_user.can()` predicates client-side from the served slot, so there `can(object, 'transfer')` follows the narrowed hint. See ③ F3.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on four packages: plugin-security, core, plugin-hono-server and spec. The BREAKING banner and the ADR-0087 marker are kept, and the marker now names the added export. `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is in the PR body and the changeset, and its sentence now covers only explain and the served slot. That is correct.

- **The added core export at `patch`** is the level the repo's changeset rule gives a non-protocol change. Accepted.
- **Spec at `patch`** for a docblock clause is accepted. The generated-artifact gates are green on this head.
- **`Metadata-protocol: none`** now holds for server evaluation, because an authored `can()` means what it meant. Re-read it once F3 is resolved. If the Console-side reading is kept and documented as the hint, `none` stands.

### ③ Boundary flags

**F1: closed.** See ① item 1.

**F3: must-fix (public text; no code change is needed if the behaviour is intended).** Two published statements are not true of the tree.

- **(a) The "unchanged" claim for `can()`.**
  - The changeset, the ADR-0142 note, the ADR Status line and the PR body all say that `current_user.can(object, 'transfer')` "in an expression is unchanged: it reads the transfer grant". That is true only where the server evaluates the expression.
  - The Console binds the served `/auth/me/permissions` `objects` map as the answer sheet for client-side `current_user.can()` (`ui/packages/app-shell/src/providers/ExpressionProvider.tsx`, `ui/packages/core/src/evaluator/subjectPermissions.ts`).
  - So for a principal holding the transfer grant without edit, a predicate the Console evaluates now answers `false`, while the server answers `true` for the same expression.
  - The direction is safe: the client under-offers, and the server never refuses what the client showed. It is arguably inside the ruling's "client permission hint". But it is an author-visible change that the BREAKING migration note and the governed text deny, and the PR body's list of `ui/` consumers omits this reader.
  - Needed: qualify each sentence to server evaluation. State that a predicate evaluated in the Console reads the served hint, and give the consequence for an author who gated an assign-on-create offer on it.
- **(b) The published schema description.**
  - `GetEffectivePermissionsResponseSchema.objects` in `packages/spec/src/api/auth.zod.ts`, and its generated reference page `content/docs/references/api/auth.mdx`, still describe the slot as "the map `current_user.can()` reads on the server". After the split, that is false for one bit.
  - The spec is already in this diff, and the neighbouring contract docblock was corrected.
  - Needed: correct this description the same way, and regenerate the artifacts.

**F2: closed as a note.** D4 now says a claim is reported by its own reason, not by the `object_crud` verdict.

### ④ Design judgment

**Spec file (schema face), `security-service.ts`.** The added clause is accurate against the code: the service map is the base map, and the served slot differs in one bit. It also keeps the "computed once" claim honest, because the request builds the map once and the slot is a pure derivation of it. The clause is incomplete only by its neighbour, which is F3 (b).

**ADR-0142 (rules face).**
- The anchor should-fix is closed. The mapping sentence now cites the two symbols that compose the answer, and both exist at this head.
- The should-fix bound to F1 is closed in substance: the note states that `can()` is unchanged. It now carries the over-statement in F3 (a).
- The D4 nit is closed.
- Against the ruling, all three carriers are aligned and enforcement is unchanged. Against the record's first consumer (claim), nothing moved.

**Is the split honest against the core module's "computed once" contract?** Yes.
- The module docblock states the split, names the carrier list, and says the two answers are equal except for one bit. The tests pin exactly that.
- There is one builder and one derivation, so there is no second merge that could drift.
- The derivation runs on a finished map, so it sees every earlier clamp. The ordering concern from the first record no longer applies.
- **nit.** The derivation copies entries shallowly. Only the one bit is written, so nothing aliases harmfully.

**Break attempts on the delta.**
- **Insert-time create-and-assign:** unchanged at the server, including an option gated on `can()`, which was the F1 case.
- **Evaluator fold and ownership step:** untouched.
- **Explain versus the door:** unchanged from the first record.
- **`*` entry and ordering:** sound, as above.
- **Hint consumers:** unchanged from the first record. The client-side predicate reader is F3 (a).
- **Another route serving the unclamped map to a client:** none found. The builder has two callers: the endpoint (derived) and the security service (base, server-side).

**nit carried over.** The core CHANGELOG entry and the spec fold's jsdoc still read as before. With the split they are true again for the base map, so no change is needed.

F1 and both should-fixes are closed. The verdict rests on F3 alone, and its remedy is text plus a spec regeneration.

security#2 · os-justin · session_01QSeKYn5CmmdShCJifm6WYj

The seat adopts the delta record below. The same isolated reviewer rendered it on this head at the contract-review tier.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `6ab383e9dbe5f5f616eb1c71817fbdc24ccdc54c`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/auth.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/security-service.ts, docs/adr/0142-ownership-queue-membership-claim-and-assignment-rules.md + packages/core/src/security/effective-object-permissions.ts, packages/core/src/security/index.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/current-user-endpoints.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/explain-engine.ts, .changeset/explain-transfer-composes-edit.md, content/docs/permissions/explain.mdx, content/docs/references/api/auth.mdx, packages/core/src/security/effective-object-permissions.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-hono-server/src/current-user-endpoints-effective-objects.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/get-effective-object-permissions.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/explain-engine.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/explain-enforce-parity.test.ts

This is a delta record on the FAIL at `4e69ae05c2` (comment 6767777433). The reviewer read:
- the delta `4e69ae05c2..6ab383e9db` (three commits, 7 files, 19 insertions and 15 deletions);
- the tree at this head;
- the replaced PR body;
- the head's check-runs.

**Check-runs:** none were registered on this head at read time (0 check-runs; combined status pending with 0 contexts). So this record observed no gate result on `6ab383e9db`. The previous head `4e69ae05c2` read 58 success, 10 skipped, 0 failed. The PR body reports the generated-artifact check at 14 of 14 locally; this record did not run it. The verdict below is on the text and the tree. The head's own gates still have to come back green before it lands.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **No behaviour moved in this delta.** The only non-prose change is two test titles; no statement of any source function changed. Every code judgment in the two earlier records stands:
   - the base map is as on the merge-base;
   - the served slot is the one derivation;
   - explain composes the two halves;
   - enforcement is untouched.
2. **The Console-side reading is kept and is now declared.** A predicate the Console evaluates reads the served slot, so there `can(object, 'transfer')` follows the hint. The seat's position is that this is the ruling's "client permission hint". That is a fair reading of the ruling, and it is accepted:
   - the answer is client-side;
   - it errs safe: the client under-offers and the server still judges;
   - the server's answer for the same expression is unchanged.
3. **Published schema description, the `objects` slot of the `/me/permissions` response (`auth.zod.ts`).** It now states the one exception: in the served slot, `allowTransfer` follows edit. That is true of the tree. The change is description-only; no shape, key or type moved.

### ② Semver level

Unchanged and still correct: `patch` on plugin-security, core, plugin-hono-server and spec, with the BREAKING banner and the ADR-0087 marker. `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` stands in the PR body and the changeset.

`Metadata-protocol: none` stands. What an author can write, and what the server makes of it, are unchanged. The Console-side effect is the client hint narrowing, which the Clause-② line and the migration text now carry.

### ③ Boundary flags

**F3 (a): closed.** Every "unchanged" claim for `can()` is now qualified to server evaluation. Each carrier adds the rule that a Console-evaluated predicate reads the served hint. Checked at this head:
- the changeset, including a migration sentence for an author who gated an assign-on-create offer on the predicate, with the consequence and the fix;
- the ADR-0142 note in Context §1 and the Status-line entry;
- the core module docblock;
- the spec `security-service` contract docblock;
- the PR body, which now lists the client-side predicate reader among the `ui/` consumers.

No unqualified "in an expression is unchanged" sentence remains anywhere in the tree.

**F3 (b): closed.** The schema description is corrected at its source. Both occurrences in the generated reference page `content/docs/references/api/auth.mdx` carry the same sentence, and no other copy of the old sentence remains in the tree.

No new flag.

### ④ Design judgment

**Spec files (schema face).**
- `auth.zod.ts`: the description is true of what the endpoint serves, and it is stated as a rule, not a mechanism.
- `security-service.ts`: the docblock now says the served slot is also what a Console-evaluated predicate reads, and that the service map is what the server-evaluated predicate reads. Both halves are true of the tree.

**ADR-0142 (rules face).** The note and the Status line agree with each other, with the ruling's three carriers, and with the code. Against the record's first consumer (claim), nothing has moved since the D4 wording was fixed at the previous head.

**Public text against the tree.** The changeset, the ADR, `explain.mdx`, the schema description and the PR body were each read against the code, and each is true. All of them stay at rule level: they say which reader gives which answer, and none describes [detail held by the security seat].

**Residual notes, none graded above nit.**
